copy: Most fitness coaching SaaS is built for gyms with reception desks. Solo and small-studio coaches are running on Notion, Google Sheets, and three WhatsApp groups to hold it together. FitFlow is being built for the second group.

Spent yesterday calculating actual COGS for FitFlow. Pricing came out: Starter $25 / Pro $59 / Studio $119. All flat-fee, all grounded in real per-coach costs. Anyone selling you "free + transaction cut" SaaS is getting paid most when you do best.

The coach FitFlow is built for: 1-on-1s and small group sessions. 30–80 active clients. ~7 hours a week on admin (rebookings, reminders, no-show chasing). Lives in WhatsApp. If you're nodding by now, this one's for you.

Mindbody charges per-transaction on top of monthly fees. For a solo coach billing $4k/mo, that's ~$120/mo to the platform before features even land. Flat-fee isn't a feature for FitFlow. It's the pricing model itself doing the differentiation.

copy: Why FitFlow is launching on Telegram before WhatsApp 🧵
Telegram lets us ship to 50 beta coaches without Meta's approval queue. For a pre-launch B2B SaaS, that's a 6–8 week head start on the feedback loop.
WhatsApp matters more long-term — that's where the clients live. But shipping the bot logic on Telegram first means we get the architecture right before we start paying per-message.
The trick: a channel abstraction layer that treats Telegram and WhatsApp as plug-ins. Same coach API, different delivery rail. Will write up the design when WhatsApp goes live.
Three concrete wins from treating the messaging channel as a plug-in instead of a platform. Building FitFlow on Telegram + WhatsApp 🧵
1/ Switching a coach between channels is a config change, not a migration. Beta coaches start on Telegram, move to WhatsApp at upgrade — same data, same bot, different rail.
2/ Channel-specific quirks (template messages, 24-hr windows, BSP rules) live behind the abstraction. The coach-facing logic stays clean enough to actually evolve.
3/ Telegram is free for beta. WhatsApp pays the bills for paid tiers. That split lets us validate retention before message COGS shows up on the P&L.

Three things solo coaches told us they hate about their current setup, in their words: "Clients ghost me if I don't follow up twice." "I can't tell who's about to cancel until they cancel." "Reminders go from a 5-digit number my clients don't recognise." FitFlow fixes all three.

The WhatsApp BSP question: Twilio for speed-to-first-coach, 360dialog for unit economics at scale. We're starting on Twilio and migrating once a coach hits ~500 conversations/month. Sharing the breakeven calc when the migration ships.
The FitFlow client experience, in one screenshot: a WhatsApp message from your bot, in your voice — "Same time next week, Sarah?" One tap to confirm. No app. No login. No friction. More next week.

If you're a solo coach, you don't have a software problem. You have a follow-up problem. Most of what gets sold to you as "fitness business software" is treating the wrong cause. FitFlow starts with follow-up and works outward.

Three things I've changed my mind about while building FitFlow:

— Coaches don't want a dashboard. They want fewer notifications.
— Instagram automation is a dead end.
— Pricing is the product, not a number you decide at the end.
